text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Street vendors in the capital run amok, smashing vehicles and looting shops after the local government authority burns their vending stalls in an early morning raid.
- The government accuses the opposition of being behind the burning of illegal vendors' stalls in the capital's business district.
- The Mineworkers Union of Zambia rejects prices at which Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) has pegged company houses it wants to sell to miners.
- An opposition supporter, charged with rioting, claims his testicles were crushed when police tortured him in detention.
- The Civil Servants Union warns of industrial strife if the government does not meet its demands for new conditions of service for its members.
